REZON fall detector · wiring list

SM-24 geophone · ADC 15 Click · ESP32-S3 · PCM5102A + PAM8403 · SIM868 (Waveshare) · 18650 · hackathon build · 2026-11-12 · same numbering as the 3D guide (Rezon_Wiring_Guide.html)

How to read a hole

  • Main board: rows A … Z, AA (27) from the back edge to the front edge; columns 1 … 35 from left to right, seen from the component side with the rails and H1 at the front.
  • K6 = row K, column 6. Lid board: rows A–H, columns 1–12, same rule.
  • On the solder side (board turned over like a page) row A stays at the top and column 1 is on the right. All maps of solder-side work are drawn that way.
  • Write “A” and “1” on both sides of the board before you start.

How every connection is made

  • Bare wire (rails/buses): 20 AWG solid, laid across the pads on the solder side, soldered at each listed hole.
  • Bridge: bend the component leg flat onto the neighbouring pin and solder both (one joint).
  • Link (33×): one insulated core from the 6×0.22 cable on the solder side. Cut to the listed length, strip 3 mm both ends, solder each end onto the named pin leg. “via” lists the corner holes the wire passes over.
  • Top wire: on the component side (screw terminals, module pads).
  • Two wires may cross (insulated); a link never runs along a bare rail.

Colours used in this list

GND5 VVBAT3V3SPII²SUARTSpeakerLED/buttonBattery senseBare wire
Colours are for reading the list. The insulated cores can be any colour; label both ends with tape if they are all the same.

Board layout · component side

Check your modules first. The ESP32-S3 rows must be 9 holes apart (B and K), the Click rows 9 apart (N and W). If one of yours differs, shift that module’s second row and every hole that refers to it. Firmware pin map: SCK 12, MISO 13, MOSI 14, ADC-CS 11, clock-CS 9, DRDY 10, ADC-RST 8, I²S BCK 4 / LCK 5 / DIN 6, SIM868 TXD→GPIO18, GPIO17→SIM868 RXD, SIM868 PWRKEY 16 (HIGH 1.5 s), button 7, LED 15, VBAT/2 on GPIO1.

STEP 2Cut the perfboard

Cutting bench

Cut the 9 × 15 cm perfboard (stock row 101) into the main board (35 columns × 27 rows of holes, ≈ 90 × 70 mm) and the lid board (12 × 8 holes, ≈ 30 × 20 mm). Score both sides along a hole row, snap, sand flat, knock 1 mm off each corner. With a pen, write “A” at the back edge and “1” at the left edge on BOTH sides of the main board.

STEP 3Sockets, headers & module pins

Soldering stationCutting bench

Component side up. Solder every socket and header before any wire. Plug the module in while soldering so the rows stay parallel; tack one pin at each end first, check, then solder the rest.

Holes

B2 … B23ESP32-S3 J3 socket, 22 contacts. B23 = J3-1 (GND, antenna end), B2 = J3-22 (GND, USB end)
K2 … K23ESP32-S3 J1 socket, 22 contacts. K23 = J1-1 (3V3), K3 = J1-21 (5V), K2 = J1-22 (GND)
N2 … N9Click back header socket, 8 contacts. N9 = CS2, N8 = INT, N7–N3 = NC, N2 = GND
W2 … W9Click front header socket, 8 contacts. W9 = NC, W8 = RST, W7 = CS1, W6 = SCK, W5 = SDO, W4 = SDI, W3 = 3V3, W2 = GND
J29 … J33H2 SIM868 header, 5 male pins pointing up: J29 3V3, J30 PWRKEY, J31 SIM RXD, J32 SIM TXD, J33 GND (the SIM868 board itself is off the perfboard, at the back wall)
N20 … N25PCM5102A: its own male header soldered straight into the board. N20 VIN, N21 GND, N22 LCK, N23 DIN, N24 BCK, N25 SCK
Q28 … Q32PAM8403 input/power pins (male header pins, module 2 mm above the board): Q28 L in, Q29 ⏚ in, Q30 R in, Q31 +5V, Q32 GND
Y28 Y29 Y31 Y32PAM8403 output pins: Y28 L+, Y29 L−, Y31 R−, Y32 R+
Z19 … Z24H1 lid header, 6 male pins pointing up: Z19 5V, Z20 GND, Z21 LED, Z22 BTN, Z23 SPK+, Z24 SPK−

STEP 8SIM868: power leads, UART, jumpers

Soldering stationCutting bench

The Waveshare Pico-SIM868 board is used as a modem only: pull the Pico H off it, it is not used. Fit C1, then the four links on the solder side to H2. Then the two 0.5 mm² power leads from L35/L33 (top side) to a PH2.0 plug for the board’s battery socket, and five M-F jumpers from H2 into the board’s Pico sockets. Before power-on: GSM antenna on the “GSM” u.FL socket, nano SIM (PIN off) in the slot, the board’s power slide switch on the battery side.

SIM868 board: what goes where

pin 1 (GP0)SIM868 RXD, through the board’s own 3.3 V ↔ 2.8 V level shifter. From H2 J31 ← GPIO17 (ESP TX). No divider needed.
pin 2 (GP1)SIM868 TXD. To H2 J32 → GPIO18 (ESP RX).
pin 3GND. From H2 J33 (GND bus col 33).
pin 19 (GP14)PWR_EN: drives an NPN on the SIM868 PWRKEY. HIGH for 1.5 s switches the module on (or off). From H2 J30 ← GPIO16.
pin 36 (3V3 OUT)Powers the board’s level shifter, microphone and RTC backup. From H2 J29 ← ESP32 3V3. Without it the UART stays dead.
pin 39, pin 40VSYS, VBUS: leave EMPTY. Never 5 V into this board.
BAT (PH2.0)Battery socket → SIM868 VBAT (3.4–4.4 V, 2 A bursts). Red lead from L35 (VBAT rail), black from L33 (GND bus). Check polarity against the plug of the Li-po in the box.
GSM (u.FL)GSM antenna, stuck flat to the inner wall at the back left. GNSS and BT sockets stay empty.
